initial.boundary: Real owner/target subprocesses and SQLite release-failure injection exposed retained capacity after complete cleanup, including a live-then-dead owner scenario.

startupContinuation.boundary: Review of the initial new implementation found that one startup page stranded a valid receipt after 128 missing proofs. A fixed bounded initial cohort now completes in the same open.

protocol.ownerDeathEvidence: ESRCH only; missing owner registration is insufficient

limits: This validates complete receipt ingestion after owner cleanup, not safe cleanup of an active orphan.
The subprocess fixture closes a real Node target before reporting completion; it is not a Guardian/PTY/OCI cleanup or Chromium/BrowserUse provider acceptance run.
Browser-session/task cases validate declared capacity scope with fixture completion evidence, not those backends independently.
Absent, malformed, partial, component-only, conflicting, legacy or live-owner evidence retains capacity.
Receipt publication performs bounded file and directory fsync while holding the SQLite writer transaction; latency has not been measured.
No automatic receipt/history garbage collection is introduced. Polluted cohorts beyond the valid 768 outstanding-resource bound require explicit bounded continuation.
